name: Autoimmune Gastritis / Pernicious Anemia

criteria.description: Presence of anti-parietal cell antibodies in serum
Histological evidence of gastric mucosal atrophy predominantly in the corpus and fundus
Laboratory confirmed vitamin B12 deficiency with elevated methylmalonic acid and homocysteine
Presence of intrinsic factor antibodies in serum
Peripheral blood smear showing megaloblastic anemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of gastric mucosal atrophy on biopsy plus either anti-parietal cell antibodies or vitamin B12 deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Intrinsic factor antibody testing increases specificity but is not always positive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Paresthesia due to subacute combined degeneration
pathognomonic.notes: Peripheral neuropathy related to B12 deficiency

common.notes: Due to decreased oxygen carrying capacity
May be due to malabsorption or chronic disease

rare.notes: Due to chronic blood loss or malabsorption
Secondary to severe anemia or hypoalbuminemia

laboratory: Macrocytic anemia with elevated mean corpuscular volume (MCV)
Elevated methylmalonic acid and homocysteine levels
imaging: Endoscopic findings of gastric mucosal atrophy in the corpus and fundus
Possible gastric intestinal metaplasia on biopsy
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; associated with HLA-DR antigens (e.g., HLA-DR3, DR4)
other: Histopathology showing loss of parietal cells and lymphocytic infiltration
Schilling test historically used to confirm B12 malabsorption (rarely used now)

distinguishingFeatures: Antral predominant gastritis rather than corpus
History of inadequate dietary intake (e.g., veganism)
Negative anti-parietal cell and intrinsic factor antibodies

redFlags: Severe neurological deficits including ataxia and spasticity
Development of gastric neoplasia (carcinoid or adenocarcinoma)
references: Anderson GJ, et al. Autoimmune gastritis and pernicious anemia. N Engl J Med. 2020;382(12):1157-1165.
Tack GJ, et al. Autoimmune gastritis: pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment. Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2019;16(3):207-220.
Stabler SP. Clinical practice. Vitamin B12 deficiency. N Engl J Med. 2013;368(2):149-160.
